source.title: SGD with a Constant Large Learning Rate Can Converge to Local Maxima
source.authors: Liu Ziyin; Botao Li; James B. Simon; Masakuni Ueda

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper's own results challenge a broad inference that SGD's implicit bias reliably favors flatter minima: in a constructed stochastic optimization problem it converges to sharper minima. Its toy neural-network experiment concerns convergence to a saddle point, not natural-label generalization.
record.gate_note: The study does not test memorization of random labels or test error on natural labels. Results about convergence to maxima, saddle points, and sharp minima bear on V7's sharpness/implicit-regularization premise, but do not measure a generalization gap or compare magnitude-aware perturbation measures. Cited generalization claims are prior work and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes optimization dynamics on constructed objectives, without measuring held-out performance or generalization gaps. Its sharp-minimum counterexample concerns SGD's preference among minima, not V7's correlation between magnitude-aware sharpness and generalization gaps. None of V1–V8 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors show undesirable convergence behavior from constant-rate SGD with minibatch noise in constructed examples, including a minimal neural network. They explicitly leave relevance to practical deep learning and effects on generalization unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: The study constructs worst-case optimization landscapes and a minimal neural-network-like example to analyze constant-learning-rate SGD dynamics; it does not study natural-label test error or random-label memorization.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate changes convergence in the toy neural network; momentum changes Adam's behavior in the AMSGrad comparison. The paper also analyzes batch size and additive noise in a continuous-time approximation, without testing generalization-gap outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: On constructed objectives, constant-rate SGD can converge to a local maximum and can escape a saddle arbitrarily slowly even with learning-rate tuning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: State-dependent minibatch noise can prevent or substantially slow SGD's escape from stationary points on constructed objectives.

fits_no_version.finding: Proposition 4 conditionally selects the sharper minima; Appendix A.4 also reports convergence to sharper minima in 2000 simulations at learning rate 0.05.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD need not prefer minima with smaller Hessian trace on constructed nonconvex objectives.

fits_no_version.finding: The minimal neural network reaches the global-minimum valley at learning rate 0.001 and a saddle at 0.1, with stationary loss rising from approximately 2.25 to 2.5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning rate can determine whether SGD reaches a global-minimum valley or a saddle in a minimal nonlinear network.

fits_no_version.finding: Adam and AMSGrad approach the constructed maximum without momentum; with momentum, AMSGrad still approaches it while Adam remains away from both maximum and minimum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Momentum can change Adam's attraction to a constructed local maximum differently from AMSGrad.

record.problems: The authors explicitly characterize the constructions as minimal and simplistic and far from practice. The neural-network example uses a single input and stochastic binary-valued labels, and reports training convergence/loss rather than held-out performance. Several outcomes are stated qualitatively or read from plots; no generalization-gap evidence is provided.
record.rows_left_out: No otherwise eligible reported results were omitted. The theoretical propositions about convergence to local maxima and slow escape are not results on the claim's generalization behavior; the figure-only escape-rate and sharp-minimum simulations do not measure any version's named outcome.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label memorization and held-out accuracy on natural versus random labels under matched architectures and training recipes.
Test error as network width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Image-classification test error for convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under the specified tuning, weight-decay, and switching conditions.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout's effects on held-out error across dataset sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation conditions.

The relation between magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and generalization gaps among convolutional networks with similarly low training loss, including comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy changes after removing highly memorized examples versus equal numbers of random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Replace the record's T5 classification and V7 tested_not_extracted designation. A counterexample to an unconditional SGD flat-minimum preference does not test V7's stated correlational claim. States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8; this does not dispute the reported optimization outcomes.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification generalization.
Adaptive optimizers' held-out performance under tuning and weight-decay conditions.
Large-batch versus small-batch held-out performance under epoch budgets.

No generalization-gap measurement, magnitude-aware perturbation measure, or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures. The study tests the related premise that SGD favors flat minima, but its sharpness result does not measure V7's named gap-tracking relation.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: SGD on the loss function in Eq. (6)
rows.operation_detail: SGD trained on the constructed two-dimensional loss; proposition states that if it converges in probability, it converges to the sharper minimum.

conditions.value: λ < c for some constant c = O(1)
there exists some b such that the stated convergence holds

rows.measure: Which local minimum SGD converges to, characterized by Hessian-trace sharpness
rows.value: Converges to the sharper minimum at (w1,w2) = (0, ±√((1+a)/2)), if it converges in probability.
rows.note: Constructed toy objective, not a neural-network generalization experiment. The paper defines sharpness as the trace of the Hessian; no test-error or generalization-gap outcome is reported.
rows.check: The conditional convergence statement matches Proposition 4, but Hessian-trace sharpness and minimum selection cannot establish V7's gap-tracking relation. The subject is a constructed objective, not a toy neural network.

rows.value: For a significant range of large learning rates, the model invariably converges to a saddle point with L = 2.5; it diverges at λ ≈ 0.11.
rows.locator: Section 6.3, Figure 3 right and accompanying text
rows.note: The loss-versus-learning-rate curve is described in text; the paper gives no numerical endpoints for the range of learning rates converging to the saddle.
rows.check: Stationary training loss cannot establish any version's effect. Figure 3 specifies divergence above learning rate 0.108, consistent with the text's approximate 0.11.

rows.subject: Adam
rows.operation_detail: Compared Adam and AMSGrad on the constructed quadratic loss.
rows.value: Adam converges to the local maximum with almost the same speed as AMSGrad.
rows.uncertainty: Shaded uncertainty region described as almost invisibly small; no numerical value stated.
rows.note: Optimizer comparison on a toy objective, not an adaptive-optimizer generalization comparison.
rows.check: The convergence description is accurate, but this is Adam on a constructed quadratic objective, not a toy neural network or a held-out optimizer comparison under V4.

rows.value: AMSGrad still converges to the local maximum.

rows.check: The convergence description is accurate, but this is AMSGrad on a constructed quadratic objective, not a toy neural network or a generalization experiment.

rows.subject: Adam
rows.operation_detail: Compared Adam and AMSGrad on the constructed quadratic loss.
rows.baseline: Without momentum, Adam converges to the local maximum with almost the same speed as AMSGrad
rows.value: Adam is no longer attracted to the local maximum but also remains away from the local minimum.
rows.uncertainty: Shaded uncertainty region described as almost invisibly small; no numerical value stated.
rows.note: The paper calls this a curious observation and suggests Adam with momentum might better escape saddle points; it does not report generalization.
rows.check: The text reports that Adam with momentum avoids attraction to the maximum while remaining away from the minimum. Calling this partial convergence to the maximum is misleading; it cannot determine any claim version's effect. The subject is a constructed quadratic objective.
